Let me build the landscape.

field_name: "Context construction for multi-hop KGQA / KG-grounded language model reasoning"

Categories (with parents):
1. "Inference-time subgraph retrieval & prompting for multi-hop KGQA" (parent root)
   - "Retrieval + ordering/merging of triples" — SG-RAG MOT
   - "Agentic/learned context construction with RL under budgets" — CLAUSE
   - "Prompt-composition ablation of subgraph elements" — Answer Path (2609.10237)
2. "Graph-augmented language models / structural reasoning modules" (root)
   - "Subgraph reasoning modules on PTLMs" — GreaseLM/MHGRN
   - "Graph-text memory synchronization" — Co-E
   - "Sparse-KG prompting/extrapolation" — GIVE
   - "Topology-aware graph prompting" — arxiv:2604.12503
3. "Training-time supervision for KG reasoning" (root)
   - "Latent-path / variational training from QA pairs" — Variational Reasoning (2018)
   - "RL + CoT over structured query formalisms" — STRuCT-LLM
   - "Embedding-based multi-hop KGQA training" — EmbedKGQA
   - "Knowledge-in-context for KG completion (LLM)" — KICGPT
   - "Proposed: context-enriched triple/path supervision (+repair loop, +low-hop RL)" — idea position
4. "Knowledge graph completion / link prediction" — KICGPT, EmbedKGQA

Hmm, EmbedKGQA is KGQA. Let me restructure:

Root categories:
A. "Context construction at inference time (retrieval/prompting/agents)"
   A1. "Subgraph retrieval with merging/ordering" [SG-RAG MOT]
   A2. "Learned/agentic context engineering under resource budgets" [CLAUSE]
   A3. "Controlled prompt-composition ablations" [Answer Path arxiv:2609.10237]
   A4. "Training-free graph-text memory co-evolution" [Co-E]
B. "Knowledge-augmented LM architectures (training the reader with a graph module)"
   B1. "Subgraph reasoning modules fused with PTLMs" [GreaseLM/MHGRN]
   B2. "Embedding-based multi-hop KGQA (KB embeddings + question)" [EmbedKGQA]
   B3. "Latent-path variational training from QA pairs" [Variational Reasoning]
   B4. "Sparse-KG prompt extrapolation" [GIVE]
C. "RL-based training for structured/graph reasoning"
   C1. "RL over executable query formalisms (SQL/Cypher)" [STRuCT-LLM]
   C2. "RL over context-selection policies" [CLAUSE]
D. "Training-time supervision-signal design for KG reasoning (idea's category)"
   D1. "Triple/path-only supervision (implicit status quo)" 
   D2. "Knowledge-in-context for KG completion" [KICGPT]
   D3. "Proposed: same-passage context-enriched supervision + repair loop + low-hop RL" [idea]

idea_position: "D3 - training-time supervision-signal design; specifically context-enriched triple/path supervision, which no analyzed paper occupies; the closest are inference-time context construction (A1-A3) and RL policy training (C)."

dominant_approaches: inference-time subgraph retrieval/prompting; graph-augmented LM modules; embeddings; RL for structured parsing/agent policies.

common_assumptions: 
- Local KG subgraph is the right evidence container for multi-hop.
- More/better context improves accuracy (challenged).
- Answer selection over a candidate set or a reader LM; frozen LLM in most methods.
- Gold/reasoning paths can be obtained (SPARQL, path supervision).
- Multi-hop = composition of typed edges; hop depth is the difficulty axis.
- KG incompleteness/noise is handled by retrieval or embeddings rather than repaired supervision.

common_datasets: MetaQA, WebQuestionsSP, ComplexWebQuestions, HotpotQA, FactKG, CommonsenseQA, OpenbookQA, CR-LT-KGQA, PubmedQA/BioASQ/Processbank (GIVE).

common_benchmarks: MetaQA 2/3-hop, WebQSP, CWQ, HotpotQA, FactKG, CommonsenseQA/OpenbookQA, KGC benchmarks.

common_metrics: Hits@1/answer accuracy, EM@1, F1, latency/token budget, edge growth.

repeated_limitations (LinkedFinding with paper_ids):
- Context is constructed/curated at inference; the language model's training supervision is not the object of study. [SG-RAG MOT, CLAUSE, Co-E, Answer Path, GreaseLM]
- No per-hop-depth breakdown or shallow-to-deep transfer analysis. [CLAUSE (only 2-hop headline), STRuCT-LLM, EmbedKGQA, SG-RAG MOT]
- KG context is trusted as-is; no repair of noisy/incomplete base facts in the training loop (GIVE extrapolates, EmbedKGQA predicts links). [GIVE, EmbedKGQA, Co-E]
- Evaluated on a narrow benchmark set, often MetaQA only. [SG-RAG MOT]
- Abstract-only or inaccessible evidence limited verification for some works. [KICGPT]

contradictions (LinkedFinding):
- "More context helps" vs controlled finding that non-answer-path triples contribute ~0 and syntax/order/size flat at multi-hop depth [SG-RAG MOT/CLAUSE vs Answer Path]. Note: SG-RAG MOT says merging/ordering helps; Answer Path says order/syntax flat. Direct tension.
- Over-retrieval hurts (CLAUSE: distractors depress accuracy) vs context enrichment premise (add triples).
- Training-free Co-E competitive with trained systems vs trained systems like EmbedKGQA claim SOTA — suggests training may not be necessary / the benefit of training-time supervision is questionable.

underexplored_combinations:
- Training-time context-enriched supervision (vs inference) with matched-budget controls.
- Combining an adaptive repair loop for one-hop failures with context-enriched supervision.
- Low-hop-only RL with explicit hop-depth transfer measurement.
- Same-passage/text-grounded context for standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks (most use KG-neighborhood retrieval).
- Per-hop error attribution (one-hop failure rate) as a training diagnostic.

input.field_name: Context construction and supervision for multi-hop knowledge-graph question answering

categories.name: Inference-time context construction (retrieval, prompting, agents)

categories.description: Retrieve a local subgraph with Cypher/SPARQL, deduplicate/merge overlapping triplets, and impose an order before prompting.
categories.name: Subgraph retrieval with merging and ordering

categories.description: Treat context construction as a sequential decision process and learn the selection policy (e.g., constrained multi-agent RL) with latency/token budgets.
categories.name: Learned/agentic context engineering under resource budgets

categories.description: Systematically vary which triples, syntax, order, and grounding instruction enter the prompt, using gold subgraphs to remove retriever variance.
categories.name: Controlled prompt-composition ablation

categories.description: Maintain synchronized textual and relational working memory during reasoning, extracting triples from text and injecting graph facts back into generation.
categories.name: Training-free graph-text memory co-evolution

categories.name: Subgraph reasoning modules fused with pretrained language models

input.idea_position: The idea sits in the 'Training-time supervision-signal design for KG reasoning' category, and specifically in an empty sub-category (same-passage context-enriched triple/path supervision + repair loop + low-hop RL). Every analyzed high-relevance work instead occupies the 'Inference-time context construction' category (SG-RAG MOT, CLAUSE, the answer-path prompt study, Co-E) or the 'Knowledge-augmented LM architectures' / 'KG-embedding' categories. The closest neighbors are inference-time subgraph curation (A1-A3) and RL policy training (C2); no analyzed paper changes the fine-tuning supervision signal by adding same-passage context triples, and none reports hop-depth transfer from shallow-only training.
dominant_approaches: Retrieve/assemble a local KG subgraph and prompt a frozen or lightly adapted LLM (SG-RAG MOT, CLAUSE, Co-E, answer-path study)
Fuse a KG subgraph with a pretrained language model through a dedicated graph module (GreaseLM/MHGRN)
Use KG embeddings and missing-link prediction to cope with sparsity (EmbedKGQA)
Learn context selection or query parsing with RL under rewards/budgets (CLAUSE, STRuCT-LLM)
Training-free prompting that builds or extrapolates a relational context around the query (GIVE, Co-E)
common_assumptions: A bounded local subgraph of triples is the right evidence container for multi-hop questions.
Adding relevant KG triples to the model's context improves multi-hop accuracy (explicitly challenged by the answer-path study and by CLAUSE's over-retrieval finding).
The reader model or its training supervision need not change; most methods operate on context at inference.
Reasoning paths / gold subgraphs are obtainable (gold SPARQL, path supervision) and can be used for training or evaluation.
Hop depth (chain length) is the primary difficulty axis of multi-hop QA.
KG incompleteness and noise are handled by retrieval, extrapolation, or embeddings rather than by repairing the training supervision.
Answer accuracy on standard benchmarks (MetaQA/WebQSP/CWQ/CommonsenseQA) is the primary success criterion, sometimes with latency/token budgets.
common_benchmarks: Knowledge graph completion (standard KGC benchmarks, names not retrieved for KICGPT)

repeated_limitations.description: Context is constructed or curated at inference; the language model's training supervision is not the manipulated variable, so it is untested whether a better training signal (not better retrieval) is what multi-hop KGQA needs.
No per-hop-depth breakdown or explicit shallow-to-deep transfer measurement; results are reported at aggregate or single-depth level (e.g., MetaQA-2-hop headline, zero-shot KGQA gain only +1.7%).
Base facts are trusted as-is: sparsity/noise is compensated by extrapolation, retrieval, or link prediction, and errors are not detected and repaired in a training loop.
Evaluation is often on a single benchmark or narrow domain (e.g., MetaQA only; UMLS/ConceptNet; CommonsenseQA/OpenbookQA), limiting generality of the claims.
Inaccessible or missing evidence (no abstract/full text) prevents verification of method and result overlap for some works.

Training-based approaches either use large models/heavy RL infrastructure or use latent variables rather than explicit context supervision, making them hard to compare against lightweight context-enriched fine-tuning.

contradictions.description: Ordering/merging triplets is claimed to improve answer precision (SG-RAG MOT), whereas a controlled study finds that syntax, triple order, and subgraph size produce no measurable effect at multi-hop depth; only the presence of the answer path matters.

The proposed direction assumes that adding surrounding context triples helps, but the answer-path study finds that replacing all non-chain triples with unrelated-entity material changes multi-hop accuracy by only +0.003 F1, and CLAUSE finds over-retrieval and distractor triples depress accuracy.

Training-free systems are reported competitive with trained systems (Co-E), while trained/embedding-based systems claim state-of-the-art gains (EmbedKGQA, GreaseLM), leaving unclear how much headroom specifically belongs to training-time supervision versus inference-time context.

EmbedKGQA treats KG incompleteness as the central obstacle to multi-hop KGQA, while inference-time context methods largely assume the needed triples can be retrieved or extrapolated at query time; the two framings imply different remedies (link repair vs context construction).

underexplored_combinations: Training-time context-enriched supervision for multi-hop KGQA under a matched supervision-token budget, compared directly against triple/path-only fine-tuning of the same model.
Same-source-passage (text-aligned) context triples for standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks, most of which use KG-neighborhood retrieval rather than passage-grounded context.
Combining an adaptive one-hop failure detector/repair loop with context-enriched supervision, with one-hop failure rate as a reported diagnostic.
RL optimization restricted to lower-hop instances with an explicit, pre-registered measurement of transfer to deeper hops (hop-depth breakdown and transfer gap).
A relevance-controlled context ablation (same-passage vs shuffled/random triples at fixed budget) to separate 'more tokens' from 'supporting context'.
Separating the value of the answer path from the value of surrounding context at training time (currently only tested at inference time).

input.description: Co-E is training-free yet reported competitive with larger or trained systems, and the dominant paradigm in the landscape is inference-time context construction. This raises the question of whether a training-time supervision change (context-enriched fine-tuning plus RL) adds value over simply constructing better context at inference, and whether the contribution is a supervision effect or an inference-context effect in disguise.
input.question: Does training-time supervision enrichment add value beyond training-free inference-time context construction for multi-hop KGQA?
input.rationale: The landscape is saturated with inference-time context methods, several of them training-free and competitive with trained systems; a null or small effect for the training-time intervention would remove most of the idea's contribution.
